rationale: Both reviews converge on nearly identical substantive findings (missing helper adoption at qwen3_code_predictor.py and the 310P twin, uncited CANN tiling magic numbers, the ndim!=4 edge case, and — most notably — both independently prove the test's fallback trigger comes from the alignment clause rather than the B*N clause the PR is meant to fix), so recall and precision are essentially tied and neither hits the ground truth's specific '3-path benchmark' ask. X edges ahead on actionability: it opens with a clear verdict and severity-prioritized sections (Blocking > Correctness > Tests > Gate) with inline fix code, while Y's audit-report format (repetitive [resolved]/[claim-verified] tags, trailing unrelated 'skill candidates' section) is noisier for a human reviewer to act on despite comparable grounding.
